subject: chemistry
title: Acids & Bases Adventure 1: Brønsted-Lowry and pH
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Brønsted-Lowry acids/bases and calculate pH.
meta_desc: Chemistry — Brønsted-Lowry, conjugate pairs, pH = -log[H⁺], Kw.
final_note: You learned acids donate H⁺, bases accept; conjugate pairs differ by one proton; pH = -log[H⁺]; Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acid: donates H⁺. Base: accepts H⁺.

HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻.
- HCl/Cl⁻ is one conjugate pair.
- H₂O/H₃O⁺ is the other.

Substances can be both: H₂O is amphiprotic (HCl gives H₃O⁺; NH₃ leaves OH⁻).

Water self-ionises: 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻.

Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K.

pH = -log[H⁺]; pOH = -log[OH⁻]. pH + pOH = 14 at 298 K.

Pure water: [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷; pH = 7. Acidic < 7, basic > 7.

Strong acids dissociate fully: HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄. [H⁺] = [acid].

Weak acids partial: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺. [H⁺] < [acid].

0.10 mol/dm³ HCl: pH = 1.
0.10 mol/dm³ CH₃COOH (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵): pH ≈ 2.9.

mcqs.q: Why can transition metals show variable oxidation states?
options: Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they have many shells of electrons.
The 4s and 3d orbitals are similar in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed without a large energy cost.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction significantly?
options: Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
Particles collide much more frequently at higher temperature, which is the main reason for the rate increase.
Mainly because a much larger fraction of collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy; collision frequency increases only slightly.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.

mcqs.q: Why do tertiary halogenoalkanes typically react via SN1 rather than SN2?
options: The tertiary carbocation intermediate is stabilised by three alkyl groups (positive inductive effect), making the SN1 pathway favourable.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN1 because they are more reactive in every way.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
